rows.basis: Servers' share of 2025 capital expenditures (the rest data centers and networking), as stated by the CFO on the Q4 2025 call. Servers include CPUs, not only AI accelerators.

source.quote: 60 per cent of Alphabet's capex in 2025 was spent on servers

rows.basis: Share of 2024 capex going to technical infrastructure (servers, data centers, networking), a planning statement on the Q4 2023 call. Wider than servers; a floor on the infrastructure share, not on AI.

source.quote: at least 90% of 2024 spending would focus on technical infrastructure

rows.basis: Short-lived assets (servers, CPUs and GPUs) were at most about half of cloud and AI spend through fiscal 2025; the CFO said "roughly half" long-lived in Q1 and "more than half" long-lived in Q2 and Q4. So the server share of the year is at most about 0.5.

source.quote: more than half of cloud and AI-related spending at the firm was directed toward long-lived assets ... the remaining spend was primarily for servers, both CPUs and GPUs

rows.basis: The CEO said the vast majority of 2025 capex is AI for AWS; a floor of half on the AI share of total capex, which includes fulfillment and transportation.

source.quote: The vast majority of that capex spend is on AI for AWS

rows.basis: AI-related capex including infrastructure, as stated by the CFO on the Q4 2024 call; the wording leaves open whether it is the year or cumulative, so a floor.

source.quote: total AI-related capex, including infrastructure, is now more than $5 billion

rows.basis: The vast majority of fiscal 2026 capex is revenue-generating data center equipment, per the company's plan; a floor of half on the data-center share.

source.quote: vast majority of it dedicated to revenue-generating data center equipment
